items.explains: An animated star pattern constructed in code (octagon and square tiling, Hankin contact lines) that draws itself outward, turns slowly and settles to a faint texture behind a scene.
items.action: An arabic-type scene asks for it with backdrop "girih"; in code, mount <Backdrop kind="girih" colour=... speed=... density=.../> from engine/src/looks behind the scene content. It is a scene option, not a manifest key of its own.
useWhen: A reflective or calm Arabic text scene wants a quiet geometric ground that moves slowly.
A style or scene that already accepts a backdrop name needs a decorative layer with no letters in it.
avoidWhen: The scene is busy or the pattern would compete with small text: keep it at its faint resting opacity.
The text is a quoted verse that must carry no other effect.
requirements: Decoration only: it draws nothing under the safe-zone probe and carries no text, so it never counts as content.
Only arabic-type scenes take a backdrop name today: backdrop "girih" on that scene, beside plain, sunburst and paper.
Choose a line colour with enough contrast to be seen yet quiet: it settles to 15% opacity.
The pattern is pure geometry with seeded timing, so a frame depends only on the frame number and the props.

display.explains: خلفية نجوم هندسية بتترسم من النص لبره وبعدين تهدى وتبقى خيال خفيف.
display.useWhen: لمشهد نص هادي محتاج أرضية زخرفية بتتحرك ببطء.
display.avoidWhen: لو المشهد زحمة أو الكلام صغير والنقش هيزاحمه.

items.explains: Sixteen rays in two tones of the style ground, tinted toward its accent, turning slowly behind a scene. It is a layer of its own: nothing is applied to the scene.
items.action: An arabic-type scene takes it with data.backdrop "sunburst" (the editor offers it in the scene form). Elsewhere mount <Backdrop kind="sunburst" colour=... ground=... speed=.../> behind the scene content from engine/src/looks. Not a manifest key.
useWhen: A bold, positive or announcement text scene wants a calm moving ground behind a big Arabic headline.
A single word or short phrase carries the scene and the rays can frame it.
avoidWhen: The scene is busy or carries small text: the rays compete with it.
A reflective or formal mood: use girih or the plain ground.
requirements: Decoration only: it draws nothing under the safe-zone probe and carries no text, so it never counts as content.

The two tones are the style background mixed 20 percent and 8 percent toward its accent: text that reads on the ground reads on every ray, checked on every registered style (the accent keeps 3 to 1 where it had it). The rays always turn: the rotation starts at 7.5 degrees and is never zero.

The rays turn 3 degrees a second at speed 1; a frame depends only on the frame number and the props. A frame of the render costs about 0.05 to 0.12 s more than the plain scene (the effect chain re-runs each frame as the rays turn).
Renders pin the software GL backend (scripts/lib/render-gl.mjs); the live preview in a normal browser draws the same rays.

display.explains: أشعة شمس بلونين من لون الستايل بتلف ببطء ورا نص كبير.
display.useWhen: لمشهد نص عريض وإيجابي أو إعلان.
display.avoidWhen: لو المشهد زحمة أو الكلام صغير، أو الجو هادي ورسمي.

items.explains: A fine paper grain (fibre and a faint speckle, no folds) multiplied over the scene ground, so the style background keeps its colour and gains a printed-paper texture.
items.action: An arabic-type scene takes it with data.backdrop "paper" (the editor offers it in the scene form). Elsewhere mount <Backdrop kind="paper"/> behind the scene content from engine/src/looks. Not a manifest key.
useWhen: A calm, crafted or editorial text scene on a light or cream style wants a tactile ground.
A quote or a single reflective sentence deserves a printed-page feel.
avoidWhen: A dark style: the grain is almost invisible and the ground only gets a little darker.
The scene is busy: the texture adds noise behind small text.
requirements: Decoration only: it draws nothing under the safe-zone probe and carries no text.

It is a white sheet of paper grain multiplied over the ground: the ground keeps its hue and is at most 17 percent darker anywhere (10 percent on average); checked on every registered style that text keeps its contrast.
Nothing depends on the frame: the sheet is drawn once and kept, so it costs almost nothing per frame after the first frame, which takes 2 to 4 seconds in each render tab.
Renders pin the software GL backend (scripts/lib/render-gl.mjs) because the paper shader draws different pixels on a GPU.

display.explains: ملمس ورق خفيف فوق خلفية المشهد، فاللون يفضل زي ما هو ويبان كأنه مطبوع.
display.useWhen: لمشهد نص هادي على ستايل فاتح أو كريمي.
display.avoidWhen: لو الستايل غامق (الملمس هيختفي) أو المشهد زحمة.

items.explains: An instantaneous framing step gives an existing recorded moment a distinct accent.
items.action: Place a held key one frame before the cue and a larger-scale camera key on it, then hold or return.
useWhen: A deliberate hard framing accent supports a supplied spoken point.
avoidWhen: A smooth approach is required.
The cue has no preceding frame or repeated jumps would distract.
requirements: punchStep is a camera-track helper, not a direct scene family or a source edit.
atFrame must be >= 1 and the target scale must exceed the starting scale.
Use the normal 1.03-1.07 range, preserve head and screen clearance, and retain source speed.
A framing jump is not proof, a before/after result or an explanatory mechanism.

display.explains: يأكد اللحظة بتكبير مفاجئ بسيط.
display.useWhen: مع تأكيد يستحمل قطعة في الكادر.
display.avoidWhen: لو المطلوب حركة ناعمة أو الكادر ضيق.

items.explains: Gradual framing emphasis on an existing recorded subject, without explaining a new relationship.
items.action: Author camera-track keys that ease from the existing scale to a slightly closer view, then hold or release.
useWhen: A reflective spoken point benefits from sustained visual attention.
The source has a verified safe face or screen crop.
avoidWhen: A diagram or evidence comparison must explain the claim.
The push would cross a cut or hide source details.
requirements: This is a track-authoring helper, not a selectable scene family; convert its keys into the normal camera track.
slowPush requires toFrame > fromFrame; emphasisPunch needs earlier push frames and holdFrames > releaseFrames.
Normal punches are 1.03-1.07; the 1.10 hard ceiling requires the explicit allowHard helper option.
Use reviewed source cues for speech emphasis and inspect actual head/screen framing while preserving source speed.

display.explains: يقرب الكادر بهدوء على نفس الموضوع.
display.avoidWhen: لما المعنى محتاج رسم أو دليل.

items.explains: A short scale ramp accents a moment already present in the recording.
items.action: End a small camera scale increase on the chosen cue; snapIn uses a four-frame ramp by default.
useWhen: A concise recorded term or demonstrated detail needs one crisp accent.
avoidWhen: The passage needs quiet sustained reading.
The ramp would crop the face or meaningful UI.
requirements: snap-in authors camera-track keys; it is not a scene family.
snapIn requires integer rampFrames >= 2, enough frames before atFrame, and target scale above the starting scale.
Keep normal punches within 1.03-1.07 and verify the anchor against source framing.
The ramp does not alter speech speed or supply missing explanatory content.

display.explains: يقرب الكادر بسرعة خفيفة عند نقطة مهمة.
display.useWhen: مع كلمة أو تفصيلة تستاهل تأكيد.
display.avoidWhen: لو الكادر ضيق أو الشرح هادي جدًا.

items.explains: One slow, eased push-in across the whole scene draws the eye inward without a cut.
items.action: Set the scene camera to dolly; it pushes in from rest to 1.04 (soft), 1.08 (normal) or 1.14 (strong) across the scene.
useWhen: A single graphic holds the screen for several seconds and the claim should feel like it is closing in.
A calm or serious beat benefits from sustained attention without a new element.
avoidWhen: The scene is shorter than about two seconds; the push has no time to read as a move.
Small text sits near the frame edge; the push crops it by the end.
The same scene already carries a snap-zoom, orbit or handheld (one move per scene).
requirements: Takeover (full-frame) and split scenes only: on a split scene the move acts on the graphics panel alone, clipped at the seam, while the presenter window, captions and head gates stay still. Presenter scenes keep the camera track and the head gates, and the manifest refuses a scene camera on them.
Not on one-shot, screen-recording or screen-focus, which already move their own camera.
strength is soft, normal (default) or strong; the move runs across the whole scene and ends closer than it starts.
The safe-zone probe ignores camera motion, so the resting layout must already pass; keep small text off the edges.

display.explains: اقتراب هادي ومستمر طول المشهد من غير قطع.
display.useWhen: مع مشهد جرافيك واقف كام ثانية وعايزين نشد العين ناحيته.
display.avoidWhen: لو المشهد قصير أو فيه كلام صغير قريب من الحافة.

items.explains: A seeded organic shake makes a flat graphic scene feel filmed by hand, and repeats exactly on every render.
items.action: Set the scene camera to handheld; the shake is seeded by the scene id and scaled to cover its own edges.
useWhen: A documentary, raw or energetic feel is wanted on an otherwise static graphic.
The scene is a reveal or result where a living frame helps.
avoidWhen: Dense or small text must stay perfectly steady to be read.
Evidence, numbers or comparisons must be judged precisely.
Strong strength on a long scene; the shake becomes tiring.
requirements: Takeover (full-frame) and split scenes only: on a split scene the move acts on the graphics panel alone, clipped at the seam, while the presenter window, captions and head gates stay still. Presenter scenes keep the camera track and the head gates, and the manifest refuses a scene camera on them.
Not on one-shot, screen-recording or screen-focus, which already move their own camera.
strength soft (breathing), normal (default, hand-held) or strong (walking); the frame is scaled up just enough that the shake never exposes an edge.
The safe-zone probe ignores camera motion, so the resting layout must already pass; keep small text off the edges.

display.explains: اهتزاز خفيف طبيعي يحسّسك إن المشهد مصوّر بالإيد.
display.useWhen: لما عايزين إحساس حيّ على مشهد واقف.
display.avoidWhen: لو الكلام صغير ومحتاج يفضل ثابت أو في أرقام للمقارنة.

items.explains: The view arcs slowly round a flat graphic scene, giving a still composition depth without changing what it says.
items.action: Set the scene camera to orbit; it sweeps the yaw from one side to the other across the scene (3, 5 or 8 degrees each way) and is upright in the middle.
useWhen: A single graphic or diagram holds the screen for several seconds and needs depth.
A reflective or editorial moment where life is wanted but no new information.
avoidWhen: Text near the frame edge must stay square; the turn keystones it.
The scene is short; the sweep has no time to read as one smooth move.
Two charts or numbers must be compared precisely; the tilt distorts the comparison.
requirements: Takeover (full-frame) and split scenes only: on a split scene the move acts on the graphics panel alone, clipped at the seam, while the presenter window, captions and head gates stay still. Presenter scenes keep the camera track and the head gates, and the manifest refuses a scene camera on them.
Not on one-shot, screen-recording or screen-focus, which already move their own camera.
strength soft, normal (default) or strong; the frame is scaled up just enough that the turn never exposes an edge (up to about 1.07 at strong).
The safe-zone probe ignores camera motion, so the resting layout must already pass; keep small text off the edges.

display.explains: الكاميرا بتلف ببطء حوالين المشهد وتدّي عمق من غير ما تغيّر الكلام.
display.useWhen: مع مشهد جرافيك واقف كام ثانية ومحتاج حياة.
display.avoidWhen: لو الكلام قريب من الحافة أو في أرقام بتتقارن بدقة.

items.explains: A sudden punch-in on a cue gives one beat of a graphic scene a hard accent, then settles back so the scene ends uncropped.
items.action: Set the scene camera to snap-zoom and put at on the scene frame of the beat; it lands within about four frames, holds, and relaxes within a second.
useWhen: One moment of a full-frame graphic scene deserves a hard accent, such as a figure landing or a keyword appearing.
The beat is known: a reviewed word or an authored reveal frame.
avoidWhen: More than one accent would fall in the same scene; it would pulse like a strobe.
Small text sits near the frame edge; the punch crops it for a moment.
The cue is within a second of the scene end; there is no time to relax.
requirements: Takeover (full-frame) and split scenes only: on a split scene the move acts on the graphics panel alone, clipped at the seam, while the presenter window, captions and head gates stay still. Presenter scenes keep the camera track and the head gates, and the manifest refuses a scene camera on them.
Not on one-shot, screen-recording or screen-focus, which already move their own camera.
at is a scene frame inside the scene (0 up to the last frame); left out, the cue lands 40 percent into the scene. Peak scale is 1.05 (soft), 1.10 (normal, default) or 1.18 (strong).
The safe-zone probe ignores camera motion, so the resting layout must already pass; keep small text off the edges.

display.explains: زووم مفاجئ على لحظة واحدة وبعدها المشهد يرجع لحجمه.
display.useWhen: مع لحظة واحدة في مشهد جرافيك محتاجة نبرة قوية.
display.avoidWhen: لو في أكتر من ضربة في نفس المشهد أو الكلام الصغير قريب من الحافة.

items.explains: Colour identifies one word in the existing literal caption stream.
items.action: Apply readable theme accent ink to the caption word selected by sourceIndex without changing its text or cue.
useWhen: One reviewed recorded keyword should stand out in a stable caption.
avoidWhen: The intended words were never recorded.
A highlighted subtitle would replace an explanation the viewer needs.
requirements: Use captions.emphasis with an in-range recorded sourceIndex; entries must increase strictly and allow one kind per word.
Preserve reviewed caption words, timing and reviewer attribution; do not manufacture words in graphics mode.
The renderer shifts accent ink for contrast against the caption surface.

display.explains: يلون كلمة من الكابشن المراجع.
display.avoidWhen: لو الكلمة مش موجودة في التسجيل.

items.explains: A brief scale pulse accents one existing recorded caption word.
items.action: Start that word at scale 1.12 and settle to 1 over four frames using readable accent ink.
useWhen: An energetic recorded keyword warrants a brief pulse and has room around it.
avoidWhen: The style keeps caption pills static, including section-deck and documentary.
The point needs low-motion reading or the word is not recorded.
requirements: Use one valid reviewed sourceIndex per caption emphasis entry in strictly increasing order.
captionEmphasisIssues rejects pop for every style with defaults.staticCaptions; consult current style metadata.
The pulse changes an existing recorded word only and does not add dialogue or a source-free transcript.

display.explains: يدي كلمة الكابشن نبضة سريعة.
display.useWhen: مع كلمة قوية وستايل يسمح بالحركة.
display.avoidWhen: مع captions ثابتة أو كلمة متخيلة.

items.explains: An underline marks a recorded caption word without moving the line.
items.action: Draw a theme-coloured underline under the selected sourceIndex while retaining normal word colour.
useWhen: A recorded qualification or condition needs calm typographic emphasis.
avoidWhen: Unrecorded labels are being passed off as subtitles.
Underlining adjacent words would obscure the caption.
requirements: Select one in-range reviewed sourceIndex per emphasis entry in strictly increasing order.
Underline thickness and offset follow caption font size; inspect Arabic joins and neighbouring words.
This preserves the literal caption stream and cannot create a graphics-only transcript.

display.explains: يحط خط تحت كلمة مسجلة.
display.useWhen: مع شرط أو مصطلح محتاج تأكيد هادي.
display.avoidWhen: لو الخطوط هتزحم الكابشن.

items.explains: A directional mask introduces incoming graphics at a scene boundary.
items.action: Reveal through ClipReveal inside the split graphics panel or full takeover canvas without moving the source.
useWhen: A clean graphic entrance should preserve stable presenter framing and video decode.
avoidWhen: The requested action is a before/after comparison of the same subject.
The style-owned scene forbids shared transitions.
requirements: Put kind: clip-wipe in transitions exactly on the incoming scene first frame and finish within it.
Use one graphics entrance per scene; dir accepts rtl/ltr/up/down and manifest duration is 1-120 frames.
This is an entrance mask, not evidence-wipe, an object morph or an explanatory comparison.

display.explains: يكشف الجرافيك الجديد في اتجاه واضح.
display.avoidWhen: لو المطلوب مقارنة نفس الشيء قبل وبعد.

items.explains: A palette transition signals a chapter change between two supplied palettes.
items.action: Interpolate the previous and incoming chapter grounds and theme colours behind the new graphics.
useWhen: Adjacent scenes have deliberate validated chapter palettes.
avoidWhen: Either scene lacks chapter data.
A fixed identity requires a stable ground or an image crossfade is expected.
requirements: Start on the incoming scene first frame and supply chapter on it and the immediately previous scene.
Fit the duration inside the incoming scene, allow one hue crossfade per scene, and omit dir.
Presenter-only scenes are rejected; split background is bounded to the graphics seam.
This interpolates palettes rather than footage or evidence; preserve style and brand policy.

display.explains: ينقل لون الخلفية بين فصلين.
display.avoidWhen: لو مافيش chapter أو اللون لازم يثبت.

items.explains: A travelling light band accents arrival of a graphic state without proving any inspection.
items.action: Keep the graphics visible and sweep a bounded light band across them in the selected direction.
useWhen: A technical reveal needs a brief scan without moving its graphic layer.
A scene containing a capture needs an entrance without echo decoding.
avoidWhen: The scan would imply a real detection or analysis result.
It would cross presenter-only content or obscure source details.
requirements: Start on the scene first frame, finish within it, and use one graphics entrance.
dir accepts rtl/ltr/up/down; presenter-only scenes are rejected.
This is decorative illumination, not a semantic scanner, mask reveal or evidence of analysis.

display.explains: يمرر شريط نور على الجرافيك الجديد.
display.useWhen: لكشف تقني خفيف من غير تحريك الكارت.
display.avoidWhen: لو هيبان كأنه نتيجة فحص حقيقية.

items.explains: A brisk directional move announces a new graphic scene without moving the recording camera.
items.action: Translate incoming graphics with a short fade and speed-dependent smear inside the active panel.
useWhen: An energetic change benefits from direction and the incoming graphics tolerate echo rendering.
avoidWhen: The scene mounts video or a foreground recording.
A split panel requests up/down travel or the explanation needs a quiet entrance.
requirements: Start on the incoming scene first frame and finish within it; use one graphics entrance.
Split permits rtl/ltr only because up/down can smear into the presenter window.
The contract rejects video in supported screens, screen-focus, kinetic-hook foreground, Glide media or cartoon monitor video to avoid repeated decode per echo.
Apply it to graphics; it is no process, comparison or camera-track mechanism.

display.explains: يسحب الجرافيك الجديد بسرعة.
display.avoidWhen: مع فيديو جوه المشهد أو شرح هادي.

items.explains: Theme accent singles out one recorded token within kinetic text.
items.action: Apply accent colour to a supplied sourceIndex without changing token text, metrics or cue.
useWhen: A literal term needs colour distinction within a reviewed spoken phrase.
avoidWhen: Colour would imply unsupported classifications or results.
The text has no recorded counterpart.
requirements: Use the emphasis array of scene:kinetic-text and select one of its literal sourceIndices.
The canonical scene derives words from cut recording and rejects removed/out-of-scene selections.
Accent changes token ink only; it is not a data classification or source-free text mechanism.

display.explains: يلون كلمة مسجلة جوه الجرافيك.
display.avoidWhen: لو اللون هيوحي بنتيجة مش مدعومة.

items.explains: A Latin font face keeps a recorded Latin-containing token legible in mixed-language kinetic text.
items.action: Use the configured Latin face for the selected literal token while preserving its text and logical reading order.
useWhen: A reviewed Arabic phrase includes an actual Latin product name or technical term.
avoidWhen: The selected token has no Latin letter.
The intent is translation or inserting a term that was not recorded.
requirements: Use kind: latin only for a selected literal sourceIndex inside scene:kinetic-text.
resolveEmphasis rejects a Latin mark on a token with no Latin letter.
It selects a font rather than translating speech or authorising branded copy.
Review Arabic/Latin/digit runs without splitting Arabic characters.

display.explains: يدي المصطلح الإنجليزي المسجل خطه المناسب.
display.useWhen: مع اسم أداة أو مصطلح لاتيني مسجل.
display.avoidWhen: لو الكلمة مافيهاش حروف لاتينية.

items.explains: One literal token receives a stronger spring entrance than the line base.
items.action: Override that token entrance to pop with the pop spring preset; other words retain the scene entrance.
useWhen: One recorded keyword deserves an energetic accent.
avoidWhen: All words would receive equal marks and lose hierarchy.
The phrase needs low-motion reading or the word was not recorded.
requirements: Mark an existing selected sourceIndex in scene:kinetic-text; use actual cut words and timing.
Pop emphasis overrides both enter and spring preset, including on a fade/rise line.
The token scale begins at 0.55; inspect its bounds and Arabic integrity.
It differs from a caption pulse and cannot create a silent-project transcript.

display.explains: يدي كلمة مسجلة نبضة أقوى من باقي الجملة.
display.avoidWhen: لو كل الكلام هيبقى بنفس القوة.

items.explains: A recorded Arabic token grows along its connections with kashida while it is spoken, then relaxes back to its plain form; the words around it glide apart and back, so there is never a loose gap at rest.
items.action: Lengthen the supplied Arabic sourceIndex at its best joining point over its spoken window (up to six tatweels, rising over 0.35 seconds, held through the word, relaxing over 0.25 seconds); the word stays one text node, its room in the line follows its current width continuously and the neighbouring words move with it, and a token with no legal joining point is drawn plain.
useWhen: One spoken Arabic word carries the point and deserves a calligraphic push.
avoidWhen: The token is Latin, a number, a name that must stay exactly as written, or shorter than three letters.
Several words of one phrase would stretch and the push loses its hierarchy.
requirements: Use kind: stretch on a selected sourceIndex in scene:kinetic-text; the word comes from the reviewed recording, never from free-form text.
Only an Arabic word with a legal joining point stretches (never after a non-joining letter, never inside lam-alef, never at the word edges); any other token is drawn plain and its cue is unchanged.

The line breaks and the type size are decided once with the longest form, so the line never re-wraps or resizes during the stretch, and a stretching word may sit on its own line when its longest form does not fit beside its neighbours. Inside the line the word takes the room of its current width (measured at every whole tatweel and interpolated between them) and the words around it glide apart and back with no gap at rest. Review the actual reach of the widest form in the line, face clearance and safe zones.

display.explains: بتمد الكلمة العربية زي الخط العربي وهي بتتقال، والكلمات اللي جنبها بتبعد وترجع معاها من غير فراغ.
display.avoidWhen: لو الكلمة إنجليزي أو رقم أو اسم لازم يفضل زي ما هو.

items.explains: A drawn underline marks a particular reviewed token.
items.action: Draw a directional underline beneath its measured bounds after the recorded token entry.
useWhen: A recorded condition should stay stable while a mark points to it.
avoidWhen: The mark would collide with another line, captions or protected face.
The label is not one of the selected recorded words.
requirements: Use kind: underline on a selected sourceIndex in scene:kinetic-text; do not substitute free-form text.
The renderer derives mark geometry from token layout and times it after token entry.
Review actual mark reach, adjacent text, face and safe zones; schema success does not prove clarity.

display.explains: يرسم خط تحت كلمة من التسجيل.
display.useWhen: مع مصطلح أو شرط محتاج علامة.
display.avoidWhen: لو العلامة هتزحم الكلام أو الوش.

items.explains: Heavier font weight gives one literal token priority without an added animation.
items.action: Use configured heavy weight for the selected token while retaining family, text and entry timing.
useWhen: A serious or quiet recorded phrase needs restrained hierarchy.
avoidWhen: The distinction needs a real relationship or measurement.
The word is invented or the heavier glyphs cannot fit.
requirements: Select kind: weight for an existing literal sourceIndex in scene:kinetic-text.
tokenTypeStyle changes the measured token weight without an independent pulse.
Fit the actual heavier text and preserve reviewed words, timing and Arabic joins.

display.explains: يخلي كلمة التسجيل أتقل في الخط.
display.useWhen: لتأكيد هادي من غير حركة زيادة.
display.avoidWhen: لو المطلوب رسم علاقة أو الكلمة مش مسجلة.

items.explains: A presenter-to-split framing change creates graphic space while retaining the source subject.
items.action: Lower the graphics seam and interpolate the presenter window toward the lower split window while caption positions fade.
useWhen: A recorded presenter passage opens into a graphic explanation above the speaker.
Both supplied footage windows reach the bottom and split lies below full.
avoidWhen: The move is split-to-presenter or between takeover scenes.
There is no recording or the descending seam would crop the measured head.
requirements: Use layoutTransitions, not a family: kind curtain, from presenter, to split only.
Duration is 12-120 frames with an earlier from-layout frame; the interval and following frame must use to layout.
Order transitions without overlap and finish before signoff/edit end.
Explicit full/split windows must reach y=1920 with split.windowTop > full.windowTop; inspect head clearance throughout the descent.

display.explains: يفتح مساحة شرح فوق المتحدث.
display.useWhen: للانتقال من ظهور كامل إلى split.
display.avoidWhen: للرجوع من split أو من غير تسجيل.

items.explains: A continuous source-window change moves between presenter and split presentation.
items.action: Interpolate the recorded window and crop between the presenter and split geometries while fading caption positions.
useWhen: A recording alternates between personal delivery and graphic explanation.
The subject remains safely framed throughout the geometry path.
avoidWhen: A takeover graphic needs an explanatory object morph.
There is no earlier from-layout frame or an intermediate crop would hide the face.
requirements: Use kind window-morph in layoutTransitions with different from/to values drawn from presenter and split.
Duration is 12-120 frames; the prior frame is from and the interval plus following frame are to.
Transitions must be ordered, non-overlapping and finish before signoff/edit end.
It changes source window geometry, not an object identity; review source aspect, framing and measured head clearance.

display.explains: يغير مساحة المتحدث بين كامل وsplit.
display.avoidWhen: لو المقصود تحول عنصر جرافيك.

items.explains: A technical-drawing finish over the whole picture: blue paper, white line work along every edge, a fine grid and drawing marks without any words or numbers.
items.action: Set the manifest root look to {"kind":"blueprint"} (editor Look tab, or the brief); captions and transition overlays are drawn on top and stay unfiltered.
useWhen: A how-it-works, tooling or process explanation suits a technical, drawn identity for the whole video.
The scenes are graphics-led and text-heavy: white outlines keep large Arabic text readable on the blue.
avoidWhen: The presenter, a product or brand colours must keep their natural colour.

items.explains: A light film finish over the whole picture: the corners darken a little and a fine grain moves across the frame, a new grain every frame. The picture itself is unchanged, so faces, screens and baked captions keep their colour.
items.action: Set the manifest root look to {"kind":"film"} in the editor Look tab or the brief. The look adds one layer over the picture and under the captions; it takes no options.
useWhen: A warm, cinematic or documentary feel fits the topic and the picture must keep its natural colours (a presenter, a product, a screen recording).
A flat graphics-only video needs a little life without changing its palette.
avoidWhen: The video is already grainy, dark or heavily compressed: the extra grain adds noise to noise.
The creator wants a clean, crisp tech look, or small type carries the meaning and the video is short of contrast.
requirements: Root manifest key look {kind:"film"}; no other option. It is a layer of its own (a Solid with a vignette and a noise effect blended with overlay), never an effect on the scene pixels.

The grain amount stays at 0.10 (the family limit is 0.12) and the vignette leaves the middle of the frame untouched: measured on a flat skin tone, the area where a face sits changes by under 1 percent and only the outer edge and corners darken (down to 0.71 at the corners).
Captions are drawn above the look and need no chip: the grain is light and strongest in the mid-tones, so a transparent caption keeps its outline.

The grain is a pure function of the frame number (a new seed every frame), so a re-render gives the same bytes on the same GL backend. Renders pin the software GL backend (scripts/lib/render-gl.mjs); the live preview in a normal browser draws the same look with slightly different grain pixels.

Costs roughly 0.12 to 0.18 s extra per rendered frame in the render browser (measured against the same scene with no look, one render tab, a loaded machine; riso costs about 0.3 s); nothing is drawn under the safe-zone probe.

items.action: Set the manifest root look to {"kind":"paper"} in the editor Look tab or the brief. The look adds one layer over the picture and under the captions; it takes no options.

The video is dark: the grain disappears and the picture only loses brightness.
requirements: Root manifest key look {kind:"paper"}; no other option. It is a layer of its own (a Solid with the paper effect, multiplied at 50 percent opacity), never an effect on the scene pixels.
Measured on six skin tones at the shipped strength: about 10 percent darker and warmer (blue about 14 percent lower on the lightest tone); white becomes a cream. Pure black stays black.

The sheet has no folds and a fixed seed and does not depend on the frame: every frame draws the same sheet and the effect chain is drawn once and kept, so it costs almost nothing per frame after the first (the first frame in each render tab takes 2 to 4 seconds; paper is the heaviest effect).
Captions are drawn above the look and need no chip: a multiply can only darken what a caption sat on.

Renders pin the software GL backend (scripts/lib/render-gl.mjs) because the paper shader draws different pixels on a GPU; the live preview in a normal browser draws the same look with slightly different fibre pixels.
Nothing is drawn under the safe-zone probe.

items.explains: A curtain in the style background colour builds from nothing out of small square cells, covers the whole frame at the cut, and dissolves away cell by cell to reveal the incoming scene.
items.action: Add a transition {"kind":"pixel-curtain","atFrame":<cut>,"durationInFrames":24} in the editor Effects tab or the brief. atFrame is the fully covered frame; half the duration falls before it and half after.
useWhen: A deliberate chapter or idea boundary can be briefly covered, in a graphics-led or playful video.
A digital, screen or tech subject where a pixel dissolve fits the tone.
avoidWhen: Speech or evidence must remain continuously visible across the cut.
The video is calm, reflective or formal: the cells read as playful.
requirements: atFrame is the covered cut centre; half the duration follows it and must finish before signoff. The default is 24 frames (12 build, 12 dissolve); the editor accepts 1 to 120.

The curtain colour is the style theme background, handed in by PreparedEdit as the paper prop; it is one Solid with the pixel-dissolve effect (about 45 pixel cells on the 1080 x 1920 frame, seeded so the same cells go first), never an effect on the scenes under it.
At atFrame nothing has dissolved: the whole frame is the curtain colour (the node carries data-cut-cover="full" on that frame).
Captions stay above the curtain; graphics under it are covered. Do not place it over important evidence the viewer needs to read.

Costs about 0.01 s extra per live frame (24 frames in all, measured). Deterministic and silent by itself: the generic transition sound cue lands on atFrame like any transition (a soft landing, never a sweep). Nothing is drawn under the safe-zone probe.
Renders pin the software GL backend (scripts/lib/render-gl.mjs).

Refused for styles with defaults.staticCaptions. Arabic remains joined; Latin and slotless words stay unchanged.

The cue is chunked and sized once with the longest form, so it never re-chunks or changes size during the stretch; the word's room and the caption box follow its current width. The safe-zone probe still sees the plain word in a box as wide as the longest form.
